summary.en: Learn how splitting, solving and combining determine both correctness and a recurrence.
summary.bn: সমস্যা ভাগ করা, ছোট অংশের সমাধান ও ফল জোড়া দেওয়ার সম্পর্ক শেখো।

practice.title: The Divide and Conquer Method: justify the decisions
practice.statementHtml: Explain why the recurrence or decision rule for The Divide and Conquer Method covers every valid candidate, and why evaluation terminates.
hints: Half-open children partition their parent interval.
practice.answerHtml:
For an empty interval, returning zero matches the definition of an empty sum. For a singleton, returning a[lo] also matches the contract. Now assume the routine correctly totals every shorter interval. A longer interval splits into two shorter, disjoint intervals covering its elements. By the assumption, each child returns its exact sum. Adding them therefore returns the exact parent sum.

Termination follows from the same interval sizes. When the length is at least two, mid lies strictly between lo and hi. Each recursive child has a smaller nonnegative length. Repeated splitting must reach length zero or one. This is a complete proof: the base case establishes truth, the combine step preserves it, and decreasing length prevents an endless chain.

For recursive maximum, keep the nonempty precondition explicit. The base is length one, and neither child of a larger nonempty interval is empty. Choosing the larger of two correct maxima returns the maximum of their union. The proof looks similar to the sum proof, but the different base contract matters on negative-only inputs.

practice.title: The Divide and Conquer Method: derive resource bounds
practice.statementHtml: Derive the time and auxiliary-space bounds for the implementations of The Divide and Conquer Method. Separate input, working storage and returned information.
hints: One recursive branch differs from two solved halves.
practice.answerHtml:
For the sum, let T(n) count operations on n elements. The base cost is constant. The general recurrence is T(n)=T(floor(n/2))+T(ceil(n/2))+Θ(1). A recursion tree has n singleton leaves and n-1 internal nodes for nonempty input. Each node does constant local work, giving Θ(n) total time. Its depth is Θ(log n).

The implementation runs its two children one after another. Their stack frames are not all alive together. Peak auxiliary storage follows the longest active path, giving Θ(log n) stack space. Counting every node as simultaneous memory would confuse total calls with peak storage. A loop can total the same array in Θ(n) time and Θ(1) space, so splitting is educational here rather than a speed improvement.

Merge sort instead spends Θ(n) merging at a level's root, giving T(n)=2T(n/2)+Θ(n). Binary search follows only one child, giving T(n)=T(n/2)+Θ(1). Quick sort has T(n)=T(k)+T(n-k-1)+Θ(n), where k depends on partition balance. These equations explain why the word recursive does not identify one complexity class.

quiz.prompt: Which sum interval has no elements?
quiz.explanation: Equal half-open boundaries describe an empty interval.

quiz.prompt: What must the combine step know for a recursive maximum?
quiz.explanation: The larger child maximum is the parent maximum.

quiz.prompt: Which recurrence describes a balanced recursive sum with constant combine work?
quiz.explanation: Both halves are solved and only their totals are added locally.

quiz.prompt: Why is the sequential recursive sum stack logarithmic?
options: Only one nested call path is active at a time
Every leaf stays on the stack
quiz.explanation: The calls form a balanced tree but peak storage follows its depth.

quiz.prompt: Which binary-search recurrence follows one retained half?
quiz.explanation: A discarded half creates no recursive search call.

quiz.prompt: Why must a singleton stop before another interval split?
options: Its midpoint is outside the array
quiz.explanation: A length-one half-open interval can recur unchanged if the base is missing.

quiz.prompt: What total returns from splitting five fee entries?
Which sum comes from an empty recursive interval?
How many singleton leaves appear for four entries?
quiz.explanation: Each of four singleton leaves contributes one.

keyPoints.bn: প্রতি কল কী ফেরত দেয় তা আগে ঠিক করো।

keyPoints.en: The combine operation determines local work.
keyPoints.bn: ফল জোড়া দেওয়ার কাজ থেকেই স্থানীয় খরচ বোঝা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Sequential child calls share a logarithmic-depth stack.
keyPoints.bn: পরপর কল চললে স্ট্যাকের সর্বোচ্চ গভীরতা লগারিদমিক।

keyPoints.en: One recursive branch differs from two solved halves.
keyPoints.bn: এক শাখায় খোঁজা আর দুই অংশ সমাধান করা আলাদা।

examQuestions.question: Show the worked The Divide and Conquer Method trace, including each rejected candidate or completed dependency. Explain the final answer.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
IntervalChild answersReturned sum
[0,2)7 and 310
[2,5)5 and 49
[3,5)3 and 14
[0,5)10 and 919

Read the trace from leaves toward the root when checking returned values. Read it from the root toward leaves when checking call boundaries. These are different views of the same computation. A frequent exam error is to show only the split tree and never show how answers travel back. Include both the interval and the answer for each important node.
